summary: Teniente Luis Candelaria International Airport (BRC) serves San Carlos de Bariloche, the gateway to Argentina's stunning Lake District and Nahuel Huapi National Park. The airport is renowned worldwide for one of the most spectacular approaches in commercial aviation, as pilots navigate between snow-capped Andean peaks before descending alongside glacial lakes. It handles a significant seasonal surge of both international and domestic tourists visiting nearby Cerro Catedral ski resort and the surrounding Patagonian wilderness.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from downtown Bariloche?
A: The airport is located approximately 13 km (8 miles) east of the city center, with a typical transfer time of 25-35 minutes depending on road and weather conditions.

Q: What is the best time to fly into Bariloche?
A: The ski season (June to September) and summer months (December to February) are the busiest periods. Winter flights offer dramatic snowy approaches, while summer provides clearer visibility of the lake and mountain scenery.

Q: Does the airport handle international flights?
A: Yes, BRC receives seasonal international flights, primarily from neighboring countries, but most international travelers connect through Buenos Aires (Ezeiza or Aeroparque).

Q: Can the airport be closed due to weather?
A: Yes, winter weather including snow, fog, and strong Andean winds can occasionally cause delays or diversions, so travelers should build buffer time into tight connections.
transport_tips: Authorized airport taxis and remise services (private hired cars) are available outside the terminal and offer fixed or metered fares to the city center. Public bus route 72 connects the airport to downtown Bariloche on a regular schedule at a fraction of the taxi cost. During ski season, many hotels and tour operators offer shuttle transfers that can be pre-arranged and often include ski equipment transport.
local_tip: Request a window seat on the left side of the aircraft when arriving from the north — you'll be rewarded with a breathtaking final approach passing directly over the turquoise waters of Nahuel Huapi Lake and the surrounding Andean peaks, often considered one of the most beautiful landings in the world.
